lens: APP FEASIBILITY AND SAFETY (adversarial verifier, verify-5-feasibility): can today's auto-bet machinery do this, with which setting, how many bets a day at the caps, does it loosen a limit, does it need information the app lacks at decision time, and is a close available for the bets it picks.
rule: First listed within 6 h AND listed EV >= 2.5%: (df.minToStartFirst<=360)&(df.ev>=0.025); read as 'the auto-bet with the trap guard at 6 h instead of 24 h'.
numbers_reproduced: MATCHES THE BUILDER. 122 bets, 43 games, 54.1 a day over a 2.256-day span. CLV +3.01% [+1.99, +4.39] on 64 closes/31 games (beat the close 71.9%); close_ok +3.36% [+1.99, +5.10] on 52/27; ROI +3.75% on 118 settled/42 games, CI [-16.2%, +23.7%]. Halves (cut after Oct 4): first 79 bets/32 games, CLV +2.70% on 52 closes/23 games; second 43 bets/11 games, +4.35% on 12 closes/8 games. MY OWN RE-SIMULATION of what the app would do (replay each bet's looks the way AutoBettor.run sees them: a CNO-list look, EV 2.5-15%, odds -200..+130, prop/moneyline/spread, a book page with >=2 two-sided, >=3 agreeing and checkEv>0, sharp not VETOED, 2 min before start at the earliest, placed at the first look that passes, CLV at that look's price): guard 6 h = 70 bets/25 games/31.0 a day, CLV +2.90% [+2.28, +3.77] on 67 closes (close_ok +3.08% on 64); guard 24 h = 106 bets/30 games/47.0 a day, +2.16% [+1.29, +3.14] on 101 closes. The 40 bets the 24 h guard adds (placed 6-24 h out): +0.92% [-1.63, +3.09] on 38 closes/19 games; difference <=6 h minus 6-24 h +1.99 pts [-0.35, +4.80] (63 vs 38 closes, 30 games). Against Novig's own last price the two bands tie: +3.29% (24 bets/8 games) vs +3.21% (37/19), difference +0.07 [-2.77, +3.35]. THE APP'S OWN RECORD (diagnostics EVERY BET, auto-bets only): since the guard shipped, <=6 h +3.04% [+1.82, +4.67] on 45 closes/23 games vs 6-24 h +1.98% [+0.69, +3.25] on 39 closes/21 games, difference +1.05 [-0.71, +3.22]; inside the study window +2.37% (37 closes) vs +1.98% (39), difference +0.39 [-1.31, +2.44].
reason: Feasible and safe in direction, but not a credible improvement of what the app would actually do, and not the same thing the headline measures. (1) MECHANISM: one existing setting, ScanSettings.trapEarlyHours = 6 (Settings/Auto-bet/Bids trap-guard chips Off/3/6/12/24, typed hours since v0.70.3; TrapGuard.DEFAULT_EARLY_HOURS is already 6, the phone ran 24). No code. It tightens a limit, so it loosens nothing (the 2.5% floor is already autoBetMinEv; price tolerance, daily/game caps, pregame-only, halt and sharp veto are untouched). (2) IT IS NOT THE RULE: the guard tests the clock at the decision look and the live EV, not the first look. Only 33 of the rule's 122 bets pass every gate the auto-bet applies at the first look (51 have no app-list look, 12 no book page, 12 fail the 2-sided/3-agree test, 5 are vetoed, 5 wrong kind, 4 wrong odds); only 12 were actually auto-placed; 64 of the 76 real auto-bets in the window lie outside the rule's set (53 had first-look EV under 2.5%, 43 were first listed over 6 h out). The headline +3.0% is carried by Tj's 28 HAND-placed bets (+4.92% [+3.37, +6.52], 27 closes, 93% beat); the 12 auto-placed are +1.74% [-0.43, +4.14]; the 82 unplaced are +1.57% [+0.24, +2.80] on 25 non-Tracker closes. (3) THE NEW PART IS NOT SHOWN: the 24 h to 6 h increment is +1.99 [-0.35, +4.80] (re-simulation), +1.05 [-0.71, +3.22] (the app's real auto-bets), +0.07 [-2.8, +3.4] (against Novig's own price). The 6-24 h band is itself positive on the app's real bets (+1.98% [+0.69, +3.25]). The cost is volume: 6 h cuts the app's real auto-bets from 34.6 to 16.4 a day (-53%) and the re-simulation from 47.0 to 31.0 (-34%); the 6-24 h band is about half of the real expected CLV dollars (about $0.63 of $1.29 a day). The one pro-6h fact is tail risk: closes 10+ pts worse are 0 of 63 (<=6 h) vs 2 of 38 (6-24 h) in the re-simulation, and 1 of 149 vs 13 of 145 across all placed bets (Fisher p=0.0007; mostly hand bets, only 1 of 45 among the app's own 6-24 h bets). (4) SIDE EFFECT: trapEarlyHours is ONE setting shared by the auto-bet, the alerts and the Bids tab. 8 of the 17 bid fills (47%, CLV +3.5% on 7 closes, +$8.79 on $16.13 staked) were posted 6-8.5 h out, and 116 of the newest 300 unfilled bids (39%) were posted over 6 h out: a 6 h chip also changes the bids, which this rule's evidence says nothing about; keeping bids at 24 h needs a new auto-bet-only setting (code). (5) CLOSES: 50 of the rule's 103 props have no close (Pinnacle's prop close is not in ParlayAPI); 39 of 64 closes are Tracker closes that exist only for placed bets (27 of them Tj's hand picks); the independent closes (13: ESPN/Pinnacle/Novig 3+ trades) are 10 from bets the app could NOT place and 3 from bets it could (CLV +0.01%). For the app's own 6 h set the only independent close is Novig's trades: 11 closes in 7 games, +1.00% [+0.14, +1.45]. Put to Tj at most as a neutral trade-off question already asked before (tail risk vs half the volume), not as a validated improvement.
caveats: No safety limit is loosened by the setting alone. Reaching the rule's own 122 bets WOULD loosen several: 22 are outside -200..+130 (21 over +130, 13 over +150, max +809), 14 are totals/team totals/other kinds, 51 never appeared in the app's CNO list (wide-read-only 24, Vigilant-only 27), 66 had no book page at first look. A literal implementation fails.

The auto-bet reads only CNO-list rows (AlertPicks.cnoChecked); Vigilant-only rows are bet only in Pinnacle-only mode, which is Off on the phone. 8 of 76 matched real auto-bets carry no 'c' in src, so the 'no app-list look' count (51) is an upper bound, about 10% soft.

Book pages are read only for the best 10 candidates (AutoScan AUTO_BET_CHECK_TOP=10), page valid about 5 min; 66 of the rule's 122 had none at first look. In the re-simulation 13 of 115 in-window c-list candidates were never checked and could never be placed.

Caps: with Kelly stakes held to the auto-bet's own $3.50 per bet, the re-simulation at 6 h stakes $57.1 a day (mean $1.84, max day $87.8, max game $33.8, 4 of 70 bets with fewer Novig dollars available than the stake, median available $57.5). The rule as defined would stake $104 a day (max day $132.2, max game $40.8, 8 of 122 short on available). None of $5 a bet, $500 a day, $70 a game binds. The real limits are the book check, MAX_PER_CYCLE 5, one bet per market, the 60 s pregame lead (5 rule bets first appear within 2 min of the start) and the wallet, which is shared with resting bids (the counters show bids waiting on it).

The re-simulation is an approximation: it over-places about 2x at the 6 h end (70 simulated vs 35 real auto-bets that were placed <=6 h out; recall of those 71%) and 1.4x at 24 h (recall 74%, precision 53%): it ignores cooldowns, wallet, per-game exposure and Tj's hand bets. Expect about 16 a day at 6 h (37 real <=6 h auto-bets in 2.26 days), not 31.

Guard-as-coded vs rule: 10 of the 70 simulated 6 h placements are entrants first listed over 6 h out (CLV +2.88% at the in-window price on 9 closes/7 games, but -0.51% at their first-listed price); the app has no first-listed memory, so the rule's 'fresh only' variant needs new code (60 bets, +2.90% on 58 closes, no gain).

Closes for the app's 6 h set are 53 Tracker (CNO books, bets that were placed: +3.51% [+2.69, +4.56], 92% beat) and 14 Novig trades (+0.57% [-0.54, +1.17], 8 games). Tracker closes come from the same CNO/Vigilant fair family that listed the bet.

Concentration: two NFL games hold 39 of the rule's 122 bets and 28 of the 70 simulated placements; dropping them leaves +3.29% [+2.60, +3.94] (41 closes/23 games) in the simulation, so it is not one slate. Everything is about 2.26 days: 3 game days, the second half is one day (11 games, 12 closes).

'First seen' means first seen by this phone: gaps of 30+ minutes with no look at all cover 53% of the 3,252-minute span (9 gaps of 60+ minutes = 1,482 min; the longest, 359 and 454 min, are overnight); 23 of the rule's 122 bets were first seen within 15 minutes after such a gap (+3.17% on 12 closes, same as the rest).

Dollars: at the app's own stakes the whole difference between a 6 h and a 24 h guard is about $0.3 a day of expected CLV dollars (re-simulation $1.68 vs $1.94 a day, both overstated by the over-placement; real about $1.3 a day); this is a safety/tail-risk and volume choice, not a profit lever.

What would settle 24 h vs 6 h: SE of the band gap is about 1.0 pt on 84 closes/37 games; to resolve a true 1 pt gap needs about 8x that (about 660 closes, 290 games, about 20 days at today's pace); a 2 pt gap about 165 closes, 73 games, about 5 days. It needs both bands to keep being placed (or closes for unplaced 6-24 h bets: shadow-log a Novig-trades or ESPN close for them) and it cannot be run after switching to 6 h without a shadow record.

Every change to which bets are placed is a question for Tj, not an action. This verdict does not say the 24 h guard is better; it says the 6 h gain is not demonstrated for what the app does and the shared setting has side effects on bids and alerts.

funnel.step: rule: first look <=6h and listed EV>=2.5%
+ the app CNO list carried it (c): the auto-bet reads nothing else
+ book page read at first look
+ sharp veto not VETOED (= everything the auto-bet checks at the first look)
